## Overview

LRP-CA-011 is the "does the letter-sound → word-reading association survive holding
decoding fixed" decomposition (#421 Tier 1). It is identical to
[`lrp-rli-ca-010`](https://github.com/dseinternational/language-reading-predictors/tree/main/docs/models/lrp-rli-ca-010) — minimal adjustment for age, hearing and non-verbal
ability — but adds same-wave **nonword reading** (`N`) as a second predictor. The
letter-sound slope here is the `L` → `W` level association *among children alike on
nonword decoding*; comparing it to `ca-010`'s slope is the review's attenuation check
(the review found a fifth-to-a-third attenuation, still decisively positive).

**The floor on `N` limits the estimand, not just the precision.** Nonword reading is a
6-item measure that is heavily floored (≈72/64/52/40% at zero across t1–t4; 80% of
children score 0 or 1 at t1). It is *admissible* as a linear standardised predictor logit
— `ca-001` excluded floored measures by *choice*, not a factory limit, and the
identifiability problem with a floored *outcome* or a nonparametric curve does not arise
here. But the severe floor is coarsening and measurement error **in the variable being
conditioned on**, so this fit holds decoding fixed only *partially*: the residual `L`
slope is only the association that remains after conditioning on this coarse observed
score, not a bound on, or estimate of, a non-decoding channel. Better measurement could
change the residual slope in either direction. Two further qualifications carry over from the
source note (`notes/202607241000-findings-letter-sounds-word-reading-association.md`):
under the revised DAG `N` is a **mediator** of `L → W`, not a confounder, so adjustment
changes the conditional question rather than identifying a pathway decomposition; and
because `N` is a common effect of `L` and other reading inputs, conditioning on it can
also **open a collider path**. Read this fit
alongside `ca-010`, never instead of it.

_Estimand: descriptive association (no causal warrant)._ As `ca-010`, every coefficient
is a latent-GA-confounded **adjusted association**, never causal. The single-posterior
"share retained" quantity is now implemented in the #421 Tier-3 joint model
[`lrp-rli-jm-001`](https://github.com/dseinternational/language-reading-predictors/tree/main/docs/models/lrp-rli-jm-001). This pair of separate fits remains a different,
observed-count sensitivity: its ratio is not a posterior estimand because the two slopes
come from separate fits, so pairing their draws assumes working independence. The joint
model conditions on a latent nonword outcome and is therefore complementary rather than
an interchangeable correction; neither specification identifies a causal pathway.

## Design

- **Four separate cross-sectional fits** per wave, reported side by side (as `ca-010`).
- **Predictors** `L` and `N` enter as standardised same-wave logits with regularising
  `Normal(0, 0.3)` slopes; age, hearing and non-verbal ability are the only trait adjusters.
- **Group** is a non-interpretable nuisance. **Missing hearing status** uses the study's reference-fill plus `hs_missing` nuisance-offset policy; the flag is fitted only when it varies on that wave's outcome-complete rows and is not a skill effect. Rows missing the focal outcome are dropped.
